not_run.opus: Not run: the OpenRouter key had insufficient credit (HTTP 402 in the warm-up).
not_run.gemma: Free substitute for the frontier LLM. HTTP 429 (free endpoint rate-limited upstream) on the first call of every puzzle, so it never made a move. Its 0% reflects rate limiting, not its cube skill.

frontier_attempts: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: HTTP 400, reasoning is mandatory and the credit could not cover it (warm-up)
nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free: 500 s and 16,000 tokens of reasoning, no answer (warm-up)
google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free: HTTP 429 in both benchmark runs
meta.earlier_run: data/results_limit5.json: 3 puzzles with a 5-move limit; also 0 solves
meta.analysis: Speed alone did not help. The three decision models answered in about 0.8-1.4 s per move but solved 0 of 15 puzzles in 30 moves each, although every puzzle needed only 4. Jev and Clef mostly repeated or undid moves (U U′ U U′, U2 U2 U2), and Luna refused all 150 requests. No frontier LLM produced a move (credit, mandatory reasoning cost and rate limits), so that side is unmeasured. An exact search solved every puzzle optimally in milliseconds on a CPU. I would use a hybrid: search or a planner for multi-step solving, and a fast decision model only for cheap single-step classification and gating.
